overview: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a country in the Balkans. Its capital is Sarajevo. It was part of Yugoslavia until it declared independence in 1992, which was followed by a war that lasted until 1995. Today the country is made up of two main parts, the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, plus the small Brčko District.

geography.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is mostly mountainous, with the Dinaric Alps running from north-west to south-east. Bosnia, the larger northern part, has forests and river valleys, while Herzegovina in the south is drier, with bare limestone hills. The country reaches the Adriatic Sea along only a very short stretch of coast, at the town of Neum.
